findings.reason: naming the publisher (the woken stream loop emitting a `fleet` event when a fleet-scoped result's revision moved since its last wake) makes the one mechanism §5 adds to `_send_project_changes` falsifiable; left unnamed a node may attach the event to its own tree-change path, where it never fires for a fleet result, and the plan's central delivery claim rests on a caller that does not run.
findings.text: §5 says "A fleet-scoped result goes to every open stream as one `fleet` event naming its key" but names no producer of that event, and neither piece of machinery §5 assigns the job to can emit it: `_FleetChangeWatch` (reckon/change_streams.py:238) only drops derived views and writes a wake byte to each stream's registered pipe, and `Handler._send_project_changes` (reckon/serve.py:2613) at its wake re-diffs only its own project's rows and returns to waiting when the digest is unchanged (`if next_digest == digest: continue`, reckon/serve.py:2686), so a stream woken for a fleet result writes nothing — the §5 done-when's fleet-event case would then be reachable only by a synthetic push

findings.reason: the node cannot size the interval from the plan, and the wrong choice turns §5's stated reuse rule into a recompute storm on the route §5 exists to fix; stating the interval's floor (at or above the measured computation) is a one-line change to the same sentence.
findings.text: §5's velocity key "rounds the window's end down to the refresh interval, so the stored result is reused within that interval and recomputed after it", but no value or range for that interval is given anywhere in the plan, and §5's own evidence puts the computation it must cover at 605.8 s for the all-project view (line 138, §8's landing record) — a fact §5 cites to justify answering 202 rather than waiting — so an interval shorter than the computation makes every new interval's key a miss and the all-project view compute continuously instead of reusing

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §5's cited symbols and files resolve in the assigned tree: `_start_check_refresh`/`_spawn_check_refresh`/`_CHECK_REFRESHES` (`reckon/serve.py:2187`, `:2183`, `:1027`), `Handler._send_project_changes` (`reckon/serve.py:2613`), `Handler._serve_velocity` (`reckon/serve.py:2702`), `_FleetChangeWatch` (`reckon/change_streams.py:238`), `docs/ui/velocity.jsx`, `docs/ui/state-loader.js`, `tests/test_spa_crew_cards.py`, and the extensionless `a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline` href (resolved as `docs/plans/a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline.html`).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of the four routes carries a forced-recompute case, a 50 ms bound, an age header, a stub-marker assertion that the recompute's own result becomes served, and its own inline negative control (line 139); the fleet-rollup, fleet-event and VelocityView cases each name the assertion their negative control falsifies.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gates log under the run directory ending in `EXIT=` (lines 140–141), and the one live measurement (§9's durations over ten minutes on srv-1006) is a production read of a durable access log, not a session scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §5 names existing production symbols and mechanism words only; it introduces no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag into prose or symbol, and carries no changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: two findings — line 136 asserts a fleet event, but no production publisher is named and the machinery §5 relies on today emits nothing when a woken stream's own tree is unchanged; and line 138 keys the stored velocity result on an undefined "refresh interval" whose period its own §8 evidence (605.8 s) can exceed.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 carries one deliverable (answer the four derived routes from a stored result, never behind a recompute) with the velocity key rule and the caller list as its sub-parts, and one verdict can close it.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §5's declared depends-on [s3, s8] matches its own text ("Build it after §3 and §8 merge", line 141); §4, §9 and §16 are named as earlier in the chain and are already done, and `reckon/change_streams.py` (which §5's write paths name as `_FleetChangeWatch`'s home) exists from §16's merge `d71859d00`.
